summary.title: Firestorm Pipeline Overview
summary.one_liner: Dougall Johnson's black-box reverse-engineered overview of the Apple M1 P-core (Firestorm) pipeline: uop and issue counts, execution units, fusion and renaming rules, and retire-queue sizes.
takeaways: Firestorm is 8 uops per cycle wide, with uops counted via RETIRE_UOP and issues via SCHEDULE_UOP.
Firestorm has about 11 integer and SIMD/FP execution units, each issuing at most one uop per cycle, plus load/store units.
Some instruction pairs fuse into one uop (e.g. adds+b.cc, aese+aesmc) and some moves/zeroing idioms are eliminated at rename, so they never issue.
The reorder buffer is unconventional: a ~330-entry coalesced retire queue of retire groups plus a ~623-entry rename retire queue.
Instruction table entries link to the counter experiments behind them, so the measurements can be verified; the author warns the data may contain errors.
summary.summary: This page is Dougall Johnson's reverse-engineering overview of the Firestorm (M1/A14 P-core) microarchitecture. It explains how instructions become uops, dispatch to schedulers, and retire, and it lists the integer and SIMD/FP execution units, fusion rules, and renaming-based eliminations. It also gives buffer sizes such as the retire queues, physical register files, and in-flight load/store limits. The data comes from black-box measurements using performance counters, with per-instruction tables linked to their experiments; the author notes the work may contain mistakes.
